# Best luxury buyers’ advocates in Melbourne

For a prestige home in Melbourne, I’d prioritise a specialist buyer’s advocate who can source discreet, off-market properties, independently assess multi-million-dollar valuations, negotiate with experienced selling agents and manage due diligence from the initial brief through to settlement.

My shortlist focuses on firms with relevant prestige-market experience, established local relationships and a clearly defined acquisition service — rather than simply the most recognisable luxury real estate brands.

One important distinction: a prestige selling agency represents the vendor, whereas a buyer’s advocate represents you. If your objective is to acquire the right home at the right price, independent buyer-side representation is often the better starting point.

## My shortlist

        –
        Primrose Property Consultants](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/t9gG41BciZUQGKGk1I9NNClVC-XSBPh3lKDZdrfwMutHVsj-2TZ-urblk7qpF-CFhWOKOecpUIQW8FoaQmuo__lydYvjqXHr6m1c_-OFJj1ijU5B4xpvKan5UddwcZczcQAR5zpz0VJIGUsA7ViXWDWKaxTMDZllgwiNSnTYVCjdUnv13NYQIoSrPd-tNqiq?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Primrose Buyers Advocates

(Best for inner-east prestige homes)

Primrose is my first firm to interview if you are targeting Toorak, Armadale, Malvern, Hawthorn or Kew. Established in 2003, it focuses on Melbourne’s inner east and Bayside, with full-service search, valuation, negotiation and auction bidding. Its published credentials include Victorian Buyers Agent of the Year for 2024 and 2025. [www.primrose.net.au](https://www.primrose.net.au/buyers-agent/melbourne?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Why shortlist it\:** Local relationships and suburb-specific knowledge are particularly valuable when the right heritage home or premium property never reaches the public market.

[Website and buyers’ advocacy](https://www.primrose.net.au/buyers-agent/melbourne)

## How I would compare them

The following is my practical shortlist by buying objective, not a definitive ranking of transaction results. The firms' public claims are useful starting points, but do not independently establish which one achieves the best prices for clients.

| Your priority | Start with |
|--------|--------|
| Toorak, Armadale, Malvern, Kew or Hawthorn | Primrose |
| Full-service acquisition and settlement support | Buyer’s Advocate |
| A firm explicitly focused on prestige properties | Prestige Property Buyers |
| Research-led advice and a selective, boutique relationship | Concierge Buyers Advocates |
| A Toorak-based advocate with prestige-market experience | Industry Insider Property |


## What should a good prestige acquisition adviser deliver?

At the high end of the market, I would evaluate prospective advocates against six criteria.

- **Genuine off-market access\:** Recent examples of suitable properties sourced before public launch, not just claims about agent relationships.
- **Independent valuation\:** Comparable sales adjusted for land size, orientation, architectural quality, condition, privacy, views and street position.
- **Negotiation capability\:** Experience with private treaty, pre-auction offers, competitive auctions and discreet vendor negotiations.
- **Technical due diligence\:** Coordination with your conveyancer, building inspector and relevant planning or heritage specialists.
- **Conflict management\:** Written disclosure of any selling-agency relationships, referral arrangements, developer payments or other conflicts.
- **Fee alignment\:** A clear fee proposal that explains whether the advocate charges a fixed fee or a percentage of the purchase price, and exactly what is included.

For general context, one 2026 Melbourne industry guide reports full-service buyers’ advocacy fees ranging from roughly \$5,500 for some boutique services to \$25,000 or more, with percentage-based arrangements commonly around 1.1%–2.75% plus GST. Prestige acquisitions may be priced differently, so request written quotes for the same brief. [invisionproperty.com.au](https://invisionproperty.com.au/blog/buyers-agent-melbourne-complete-guide-2026/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.buyersadvocate.com.au](https://www.buyersadvocate.com.au/best-buyers-agents-melbourne/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I would arrange initial meetings with **Primrose, Buyer’s Advocate and Prestige Property Buyers**\. They give you three different angles: deep inner-east specialisation, established end-to-end buyer representation and explicit prestige-market positioning.

Ask each to present two or three recent acquisitions comparable to your intended purchase, explain how they established fair value, and identify what they would do differently from a buyer approaching selling agents directly.

search_results.title: Melbourne house prices 2026: REA Group reveals suburbs tipped for biggest growth by 2031 and 2036
search_results.description:
New modelling from realestate.com.au forecasts significant growth in Melbourne's housing market by 2031 and 2036. Langwarrin leads with an estimated 25% five-year increase, lifting median property values from $875,000 to $1.14 million. Eight of the top 10 growing suburbs—like Frankston North, Mickleham, and Rockbank—currently have median prices under $1 million. In a 10-year outlook, 285 suburbs could see gains of at least 50%, with Mickleham and Rockbank showing strong projected values. In contrast, none of Melbourne’s 271 unit markets are expected to grow more than 25% in five years.

Realestate.com.au economist Angus Moore clarifies these figures reflect historical trends, not precise forecasts, though Melbourne's comparative affordability and rebounding interstate migration are likely to attract buyers. Despite market weaknesses, agents indicate increased interest and significant home discounts. However, high construction and land costs, along with restrictive tax policies, are constraining development. Political changes, particularly related to land tax and stamp duty, are also influencing buyer and investor sentiment. Industry leaders have criticized government actions that deter investment, calling for clearer financial planning. By 2036, million-dollar suburbs could nearly double to 372, leaving only 23 markets below that threshold.

search_results.title: Ferrari fan's $4.3m Doncaster East buy after 5hrs of inspections
search_results.description: A luxury home in Doncaster East, Melbourne, known as Saxonwood, sold for $4.3 million—marking the suburb’s highest sale since 2024. The sale followed an unusual private-inspection strategy, where qualified buyers received 45-minute one-on-one appointments. The eventual buyer, a Ferrari enthusiast and seasoned tarmac rally participant, spent over five hours inspecting the home across multiple visits. Though the property included car-centric features such as a four-car automotive gallery and over 2.5 tonnes of calacatta marble in the kitchen, it was its location—opposite Zerbes Reserve with unobstructed park views through floor-to-ceiling windows—that ultimately secured the sale. The home garnered national and international interest and went under contract after 24 days, with negotiations concluding over 13 days. The campaign included an exclusive launch event featuring $15 million worth of luxury cars and Italian food and wine, emphasizing the property's automotive and European design themes. The buyer, also planning to visit Ferrari’s factory in Italy for a custom car and to add a swimming pool post-settlement, was swayed by the unique outlook from the main living area, stating the experience of the park view sealed the decision to purchase. Agent Daniel D’Assisi now plans to replicate this marketing strategy for other high-end homes.

search_results.title: Victoria's new auction laws spark 'chaos' and confusion
search_results.description: Victoria's recent auction law changes, which require sellers to disclose their reserve price seven days before an auction, have triggered widespread confusion and criticism. The legislation, effective from October 1 after a grace period, was intended to enhance transparency and curb underquoting. However, critics like auctioneer Andy Reid and agents such as Daniel D'Assisi argue the changes were rushed and are generating chaos. They highlight loopholes, including the ability of sellers to alter reserve prices last-minute and buyer misperceptions about pricing flexibility. The Real Estate Institute of Victoria reported a preliminary clearance rate of 55.5% from 371 early results, with a significant drop in auction volumes—down 53% compared to the previous year. Experts predict a shift toward private sales due to declining confidence in the auction process. Despite the challenges, some realtors believe the market will stabilize as stakeholders adjust to the new system. Government representatives, including Consumer Affairs Minister Tim Richardson, defend the reforms as a step towards stopping deceptive sales tactics. The coming weeks are expected to determine the true impact of the legislation on Melbourne’s real estate landscape.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: Gold Coast luxury property defies downturn as Sydney buyers move in
search_results.description: Despite a nationwide property downturn that has reverted prices and sales to 2023 levels, the Gold Coast luxury real estate market remains resilient. This strength is attributed to a limited housing supply, robust internal migration, and affluent buyers—particularly from Sydney—seeking better value. Michael Kollosche, managing director of Kollosche, highlights how high-end Gold Coast apartments, priced between $25,000 and $35,000 per square metre, offer better value compared to Sydney's $120,000 per square metre rates. Notable recent sales include an $11.5 million penthouse purchase by a European investor. According to Colliers, Gold Coast property prices have surged 84% since 2021, surpassing Brisbane and Greater Brisbane. Analyst Michael Matusik notes a shift from investment properties to owner-occupied beachfront homes, as the city attracts wealthy buyers post-pandemic. Downsizing among affluent homeowners along Hedges Avenue is driving demand for luxurious, smaller residences in the same prime locations. This demographic shift is shaping a robust, high-end market insulated from broader sectoral declines.

- **Conflict management\:** Written disclosure of any selling-agency relationships, referral arrangements, developer payments or other conflicts.
- **Fee alignment\:** A clear fee proposal that explains whether the advocate charges a fixed fee or a percentage of the purchase price, and exactly what is included.

For general context, one 2026 Melbourne industry guide reports full-service buyers’ advocacy fees ranging from roughly \$5,500 for some boutique services to \$25,000 or more, with percentage-based arrangements commonly around 1.1%–2.75% plus GST. Prestige acquisitions may be priced differently, so request written quotes for the same brief. ## My recommendation

I would arrange initial meetings with **Primrose, Buyer’s Advocate and Prestige Property Buyers**\. They give you three different angles: deep inner-east specialisation, established end-to-end buyer representation and explicit prestige-market positioning.

Ask each to present two or three recent acquisitions comparable to your intended purchase, explain how they established fair value, and identify what they would do differently from a buyer approaching selling agents directly.
